subject: Vulnerability evidence: scan sampling methodology and rollback validation
messages:
From: Samir Shah <samir.shah@acme-payments.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@acme-payments.com, Alice Ng <alice.ng@acme-payments.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: sampling methodology + rollback validation for recent CVE remediation

Jordan / Redwood team,

Thanks for the materials you shared last week. Our security and procurement teams need a compact evidence bundle to close the SIG questionnaire items around vulnerability management for our SOC 2 review. Specifically we need:

- The exact scan sampling methodology you used for the 2028-08 baseline (how hosts/services were sampled, authenticated vs unauthenticated scans).
- Proof that CVE-2028-0142 was remediated in production (dates, patch manifest, who applied the change).
- A short summary of rollback validation steps you run after a patch (how you confirm roll-forwards didn't regress other services).
- The SLA mapping you use (time-to-triage, time-to-remediation) by severity class so we can match to our SIG scoring.

Can you provide a one-page summary and the associated artifacts (scan output excerpt, remediation manifest, and a short runbook snippet) we can attach to the SIG? Ideally we get these before our auditor kickoff on Sep 20.

Open to a 20m call if easier.

Thanks,
Samir
Security Engineering
Acme Payments

--
Attachment request: please include the exported scanning CSV and the remediation manifest as CSV/PDF
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@acme-payments.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 14 Sep 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: sampling methodology + rollback validation for recent CVE remediation

Hi Samir — thanks for the clear checklist. I pulled together a concise bundle and high-level answers below; I attached the CSVs and a short runbook excerpt. If you need anything formatted differently for SIG, tell me and we’ll adapt.

Summary (one page):
- Scan sampling methodology: weekly authenticated DAST on all production service endpoints (full crawl) + rolling nightly SCA (package manifest) on container images. For the August baseline we ran a stratified sample across services (traffic-weighted buckets) plus a 10% host random sample for edge infra. The sampling matrix is attached (sampling-matrix-202808.csv).
- CVE-2028-0142 remediation proof: patch applied to canary on 2028-09-02 (canary pass + smoke), staged rollout to 30% on 2028-09-06, full rollout completed 2028-09-10. Remediation manifest attached (remediation-manifest-acme-20280915.csv) with commit ids, PR links, and engineering approvers. Scan excerpt confirming absence of the CVE signature is in scan-report-20280910.pdf (page 2 shows before/after).
- Rollback validation: we validate successful roll-forward via the following minimal checks: health-check pass across dependent services (5m window), end-to-end smoke tests for top-10 customer flows, and metric regression checks (error budget, latency P50/P95). Any anomalies trigger immediate automated rollback to previous image and a manual post-mortem. The runbook excerpt (attached) shows the rollback and verification checklist.
- SLA mapping: triage within 24 hours for critical, 72 hours for high, 7 days for medium, 30 days for low (triage = initial owner assignment and risk assessment). Remediation target windows: critical = 7 days, high = 30 days, medium = 90 days; we capture exceptions in our remediation log with compensating controls.

Attachments included: sampling-matrix-202808.csv, remediation-manifest-acme-20280915.csv, scan-report-20280910.pdf (excerpt), patch-validation-runbook.pdf (excerpt).

If you want, Monica can add the auditor-friendly index sheet that references the exact file locations and hash values. Would you like that?

Best,
Jordan Blake
Sr. Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: sampling-matrix-202808.csv (CSV), remediation-manifest-acme-20280915.csv (CSV), scan-report-20280910.pdf (PDF), patch-validation-runbook.pdf (PDF)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@acme-payments.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 17 Sep 2028 10:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: sampling methodology + rollback validation for recent CVE remediation

Samir — quick technical clarifications to support the SIG controls:

1) Authenticated scans: we run authenticated crawlers using ephemeral service accounts with least privilege. Credentials are rotated per-build and not stored in plain text in the scanner. Results flagged in the CSV have a column "auth=true" for rows originating from authenticated runs.

2) Evidence of patch enforcement: the remediation manifest includes the container image digest and the orchestration rollout record (k8s deployment revision and timestamp). We can export a short audit log slice showing the image rollout if you need it for auditors; it's a filtered log (no privileged data).

3) Regression/rollback validation detail: our automated rollback is controlled by the deployment pipeline (ArgoCD hooks) and ties into Prometheus alerts. The runbook excerpt lists the exact alert thresholds used for auto-rollback (error rate > 3x baseline sustained for 5 min, tail-latency P95 > +200ms for 10m). We can redact absolute thresholds for the SIG if you prefer.

4) Evidence retention: we retain scan artifacts and remediation manifests for 18 months for SOC 2 evidence; shorter export bundles are trimmed to include only the auditor window.

If the auditor needs a formatted mapping to SIG question IDs, say which SIG version and we’ll assemble the mapping sheet.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Vulnerability Ops
Redwood Inference

Jordan / Kim — this is great, thanks. The attachments look right from a first pass.

A couple quick asks before I hand this to our auditor:
- Can you export the k8s rollout audit slice (redacted) for the 2028-09-06 to 2028-09-10 window as a CSV?
- Please include the SIG mapping sheet (we need references to SIG v2.0 IDs).

If you can send those two items today or early tomorrow, I can include them in our kickoff packet. Otherwise, let’s do a 20m sync tomorrow at 10am PT.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

—Samir
